text:
alice: Heads up — p99 GPU inference latency spiked for a subset of tenants on ded-pool-eu2 around 10:23 UTC. Seeing correlated PCIe errors on hosts rack7-node10..12. /cc @ben @carla
infra-bot: Alert: high p99 latency on ded-pool-eu2 (10:23). Affected tenants: T-analytics, T-research. Trigger: p99>300ms.
ben: Logs please?
alice: paste logs snippet:
```
[2026-02-12T10:23:17Z] host-rack7-node10 gpu0: pci 0000:5e:00.0: PCIe transaction timeout
[2026-02-12T10:23:18Z] host-rack7-node10 rdma: gpudirect qid=0x4f3: queue stalled
[2026-02-12T10:23:19Z] host-rack7-node11 iommu: upstream bandwidth saturated
```
carla: Sounds like GPUDirect / RDMA aggressively using PCIe root complex. Any long-running sampling jobs?
alice: Yes — T-analytics started a 12h sampler yesterday pinned to same PCIe root across 6 pods.
dave: Could be NUMA packing + PCIe oversubscription. Are pods scheduled with topologyKeys? kube shows them on same NUMA sibling.
rishi: We saw something similar in staging: MIG-disabled GPUs + GPUDirect can saturate PCIe and cause cross-tenant thrash. Short term options: throttle RDMA egress (tc), evict noisy pods, or disable GPUDirect per container.
ben: For immediate mitigation can infra temporarily disable GPUDirect at the node level? Or kill the sampler pods.
carla: Our options now:
- cordon + drain affected nodes (evict the 6 pods)
- add pod annotation to disable gpudirect: runtime env RUNTIME_GPDISABLE=true
- update PodTopologySpread to spread such workloads across PCIe roots
alice: I'll try throttling first to be less disruptive. Running on host: `nsenter -t 1 -n tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 200mbit burst 32kb latency 50ms` to limit RDMA traffic.
ben: Also add scheduler constraints: `topologyKeys: ["kubernetes.io/hostname", "topology.kubernetes.io/zone"]` and prefer nodes with more PCIe root complexes.
carla: Longer-term proposals:
- SR-IOV per-tenant NIC isolation to separate DMA channels
- Enforce MIG slices or GPU partitioning for noisy-tenant classes
- Work with vendor on PCIe QoS / root-complex firmware settings
- DPU offload to fence GPUDirect flows at NIC level
rishi: Can we run an A/B: enable SR-IOV on one AZ and route a small subset of tenants? Need infra window + SRE support.
dave: Cost note: SR-IOV + DPU adds ~15% hardware cost per rack but reduces evictions and p99 SLO breaches; could be part of Dedicated offering SLA.
alice: I'll create an RFC for the long-term plan and file an action item for node-level gpudirect disable flag + scheduler enforcement. For now, evicted pods are being rescheduled with gpudirect disabled. Monitoring: p99 dropped from 480ms -> 85ms within 3m.
ben: :thumbsup: keep me posted.
carla: Filing follow-up ticket INFRA-4292 for SR-IOV trial and vendor engagement.
infra-bot: Incident runbook update: step=throttle/evict_noisy -> status=done
alice: thanks all, closing loop.
